quarterly_data.signal: 10-Q capacity and supply: Bloom expects to continue making capital investments to expand production capacity at its manufacturing facilities in Fremont, California and Delmarva, Delaware (new equipment and tenant improvements), funded from cash on hand and operating cash flow. Cash used in investing activities in the nine months was $257.7 million, up $199.4 million, primarily due to a $197.5 million increase in expenditures on tenant improvements for a leased engineering and manufacturing facility in Fremont. On supply, Bloom says its supply of components has not been impacted to date, it has entered into long-term contracts, non-cancelable purchase orders and, in select cases, take-or-pay or fixed volume commitment contracts, and it does 'not currently anticipate experiencing supply chain shortages which would impact our 2026 production forecast'.
quarterly_data.figure: $197.5 million increase in Fremont tenant-improvement spending (nine months); investing cash use $257.7 million

contracts.signal: Bloom's 10-Q: under the partnership with Oracle to provide on-site solid state power for AI data centers, Bloom issued Oracle a warrant on April 9, 2026, and on May 1, 2026 Oracle completed a cashless exercise, receiving 1,905,433 shares of Bloom common stock plus 248,798 incremental shares; the aggregate fair value of the shares issued was $323.9 million. Bloom accounts for it as share-based consideration payable to a customer's customer: a Customer Consideration Asset ($91.0 million current and $215.5 million long-term at September 30, 2026) amortized as a reduction of revenue as the Energy Server systems sold under the Oracle arrangement are delivered.
contracts.value: $323.9 million aggregate fair value of shares issued to Oracle
